observed_fact: Willis remained atop the quarterback order; one observer charted him 7-of-12 with two interceptions, one caused by a receiver bobble and one after pressure in a play extended beyond a likely sack.
fantasy_implication: Do not treat raw camp interceptions as clean quarterback faults; pressure response remains a key test.

observed_fact: In red-zone work Willis was charted 6-of-10 and scored on a designed keeper from inside the 10-yard line.
fantasy_implication: Designed rushing can raise Willis's fantasy floor and compete for goal-line opportunities.

observed_fact: Willis had a rougher session under consistent pressure and threw an interception into traffic; Quinn Ewers also threw an interception and no backup distinguished himself.
fantasy_implication: The starting job is stable, but passing consistency and protection remain risks.

observed_fact: Achane caught a pass over the middle and later scored on a deep slant in red-zone work; he also opened the team period with a run sprung by Will Kacmarek.
fantasy_implication: Receiving and red-zone involvement remain visible, but practice reports do not yet establish his touch share.

observed_fact: After the first three practices Malik Washington was assessed as the most consistent receiver in the group.
fantasy_implication: Washington is the early favorite for the most stable receiving role, not yet a confirmed target leader.

observed_fact: Willis completed a long pass to Washington against double coverage during team work.
fantasy_implication: Washington is being used beyond short-area work, supporting a broader route-role hypothesis.

observed_fact: Douglas was heavily involved in red-zone practice, with two potential touchdown catches, two other receptions, and one drop.
fantasy_implication: Douglas has entered the active receiver competition, but one high-volume practice does not establish a starting role.

observed_fact: Bell remained on active/NFI and did not participate in the first three camp practices while rehabilitating his ACL injury.
fantasy_implication: Bell should not be included in the current active receiver rotation until he practices.

observed_fact: Proctor worked at left guard through the first three camp practices after playing tackle in college.
fantasy_implication: Left guard is now the strong opening-line projection, reducing uncertainty at one spot.

observed_fact: In the first padded one-on-one period Proctor stood up Zach Sieler and later delivered another notable run-blocking rep.
fantasy_implication: Early padded work supports the starting-left-guard projection but is not yet game evidence.

observed_fact: Jeff Hafley called Jackson's injury day-to-day and said he did not expect it to be long term; Jackson missed the August 4 practice.
fantasy_implication: Jackson remains the projected right tackle, but replacement reps and protection quality require monitoring.

observed_fact: Johnson was being trained at both outside corner and nickel during the opening camp block.
fantasy_implication: Johnson projects as a starter, but alignment and matchup usage are not settled.

observed_fact: Johnson recovered a fumble during the second camp practice.
fantasy_implication: Turnover production is encouraging but does not by itself establish an every-snap role.

observed_fact: Robinson repeatedly won as a pass rusher and run defender, including pressure after beating Austin Jackson.
fantasy_implication: Robinson is the clear lead edge; opposing-line matchup analysis should treat him as Miami's primary pressure threat.

observed_fact: Uche won two of three one-on-one pass-rush reps after reaching the backfield in multiple earlier practices.
fantasy_implication: Uche has the strongest early evidence for the primary complementary pass-rush role.

observed_fact: Moore sealed the edge against Carlos Washington Jr. on a notable run-defense rep.
fantasy_implication: The rookie is earning relevant evaluation reps, but his subpackage share remains unknown.

observed_fact: Anderson recorded an interception during the second camp practice.
fantasy_implication: Anderson is a live contender for the open safety role.

observed_fact: Anderson intercepted Willis in the end zone and was active as a run defender during practice six.
fantasy_implication: A second takeaway strengthens Anderson's case, but alignment and first-team share remain restricted or unreported.

observed_fact: Hafley described Johnson as day-to-day after he missed practice.
fantasy_implication: A short absence creates evaluation opportunity for Anderson and Michael Taaffe without yet displacing Johnson.

observed_fact: Hafley's camp structure emphasized sustained 11-on-11 periods rather than 7-on-7 work; reporting rules limited disclosure of unit ordering and alignments.
fantasy_implication: The evidence is more game-contextual than isolated passing drills, but personnel-grouping conclusions remain unavailable.

observed_fact: Both kickers made late-game situational field goals from approximately 50 and 43 yards.
fantasy_implication: No practice separation is established; continue to record distance and operation results for every available attempt.

observed_fact: Rodriguez was assessed as much more noticeable in the first three camp practices than during six open offseason practices.
fantasy_implication: Rodriguez is trending toward an early defensive role, but down and package usage still must be observed.

observed_fact: Hafley said the undrafted defensive tackle would miss the season with an undisclosed injury.
fantasy_implication: Remove Konga from opening-roster role projections while preserving his developmental status.

entity_or_unit: Kevin Coleman Jr. and Dante Trader Jr.
observed_fact: Coleman and Trader did not participate in 11-on-11 work during practice six.
fantasy_implication: Their participation status needs another dated check before it changes role projections.

observed_fact: Slowik said Miami shares the same Shanahan-tree bones as the prior offense but will change with personnel; he emphasized the run game, keeping defenses off balance, and precision passing.
fantasy_implication: Treat continuity as a design starting point rather than proof that 2025 usage will carry forward.

observed_fact: Slowik said Miami had emphasized on-the-move motion, acknowledged assignment and snap-point strain, and said the offense would be foolish not to retain a tool used effectively under McDaniel.
fantasy_implication: Motion is a confirmed commitment; penalties, assignment accuracy, and efficiency remain the decisive tests.

observed_fact: Duggan described a personnel- and opponent-driven defense using even and odd fronts, situational Wide-9 alignments, press and off coverage, and selective pressure.
fantasy_implication: Do not project a fixed front or blanket high-blitz identity before game charting.

observed_fact: Hafley said defensive meetings begin with takeaways, the first two minutes of every defensive individual period attack the football, and Miami is mixing man and zone coverage.
fantasy_implication: Takeaway process is deliberate, but actual turnover totals should still be treated as volatile.

observed_fact: Tabor said Hafley provides substantial special-teams practice time and that returners are being evaluated on ball security, execution, and ability to create field position.
fantasy_implication: Special-teams deployment is a meaningful roster signal, but no kicker or returner winner is established.

observed_fact: The official practice notebook described Achane producing explosive gains as both a runner and receiver, including a 25-yard catch-and-run from Malik Willis.
fantasy_implication: Achane's multidimensional involvement is independently corroborated, but routes, target share, and backfield split remain unmeasured.

observed_fact: Slowik said Willis and Washington had clearly worked together extensively and that Willis was confident in Washington's breaks; he identified Washington's footwork and separation at break points as the receiver's most noticeable improvement.
fantasy_implication: Washington has the best-supported current route-floor hypothesis, though alignment and first-read share are not established.

observed_fact: Slowik said Heck entered with the first-team offense after Austin Jackson's injury and handled his responsibilities reasonably well despite imperfect overall execution.
fantasy_implication: Heck is the first documented replacement at right tackle; the projected starting five still depends on Jackson's return.

observed_fact: Slowik said the line had seen the installed runs, protections, defensive looks, and pressures and was moving into refinement of combinations, technique, and handling line games.
fantasy_implication: Preseason protection should now be evaluated for execution rather than excused solely as incomplete installation.

observed_fact: The official practice notebook described Kacmarek and Traore contributing as blockers and receivers and quoted Zach Sieler saying the offense was using tight ends in multiple ways.
fantasy_implication: Multiple-tight-end usage is a live hypothesis, but package frequency and route allocation remain unknown.

observed_fact: Miami claimed rookie tight end Jeremiah Franklin off waivers from New England, expanding the camp room to six tight ends.
fantasy_implication: Franklin adds H-back and special-teams competition but does not change the projected fantasy hierarchy without first-unit or package evidence.

observed_fact: The official practice notebook recorded Willis taking a deep shot to Washington, providing another example of Washington working beyond a purely short-area route profile.
fantasy_implication: A broader route menu is plausible, but the target was not reported as complete and route depth frequency remains unknown.

observed_fact: Tolbert caught a 30-yard back-shoulder pass from Quinn Ewers for the official notebook's biggest passing play of practice seven.
fantasy_implication: The play supports Tolbert's boundary and catch-point role but does not establish first-team route or Willis target share.
